spec.template.spec.containers[0].readinessProbe:

message.content:
## Root cause

The `default/app` Service had a selector `app=app`, but no `readinessProbe`, so endpoints were never populated. Pods ran but never became ready, so the Service's Endpoint list was `app → 0 endpoints`, resulting in every request being dropped with `0/0` (ServiceUnavailable).

Evidence from the cluster:
- Pods `app-648b6f877-c2ngm/klzw9/q9sqw` → `0/1 Running` repeatedly.
- EndpointSlice `kubernetes.io/service-name=app` reported no endpoints (`app → 0 endpoints`); endpoints were unreachable at all IPs (`10.244.0.2:80`, `10.244.0.5:80`, `10.244.0.6:80` all `connection refused`).
- Deployment conditions: `Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable)`, `Progressing=True (NewReplicaSetAvailable)` — the only gap was readiness.
- In-pod check of the app: `GET /readyz` → **404**, so readiness could never be satisfied.

## Change

Added the missing readinessProbe on the Service's owning Deployment (the persistent owner, no Service changes made):

```
spec.template.spec.containers[0].readinessProbe:
  httpGet: {path: "/", port: 80, scheme: HTTP},
  periodSeconds: 10, failureThreshold: 3, successThreshold: 1, timeoutSeconds: 1
```

The `nginx:1.31.5` container already serves the `/` path with 200, so the new probe validates real readiness, and kept the 3-repetition tolerance / 10s window. Nothing else in the Service or Deployment was modified: `type ClusterIP`, `port 80/targetPort 80`, `port 443/kubernetes`, `replicas: 3`, image `nginx:1.31.5`.

## Verification (fresh observations after the change)

- `kubectl rollout status` → `deployment "app" successfully rolled out`
- Replica counts match the request: `READY 3/3`, `UP-TO-DATE 3`, `AVAILABLE 3`; conditions `Available=True (MinimumReplicasAvailable)`, `Progressing=True (NewReplicaSetAvailable)`
- Pods `1/1 Running`, `0 restarts`, no unhealthy events after the fix.
- EndpointSlice `app-42mfw` shows `Ready=True` with `kubernetes.io/service-name=app` → the `0 endpoints` now `10.244.0.8,10.244.0.9,10.244.0.10`
- All three endpoints were verified individually in-pod from a client pod: `ip endpoint=10.96.2.82`, `10.244.0.8`, `10.244.0.9` all returned `200`.
- Requesting the Service directly from an in-pod test: `DNS-DNS/IP http_code=200` → a Service-level request through `http://app.default.svc.cluster.local/` returned **200**.
- A temporary client pod in the cluster (`curl` image, using cluster DNS) independently confirmed `http to 10.96.2.82 succeeded` and `app.default.svc.cluster.local` also succeeded.

The originally reported symptom is gone: the Service now handles traffic with three ready, healthy Pods serving on the Service's own port, `http://10.96.2.82/` → **200**, which was a `0/0` and `connection refused` before.
